attribution.note: Marcus states and endorses the claims in his own prose.

semantics.note: The legislative clause omits the contextual limitation to protective AI legislation. Taken literally, the normalization also excludes research or funding laws, which the surrounding passage does not commit Marcus to excluding.

contract.note: The contract fairly restores the protective legislative scope and gives ordinary contextual readings to the emphatic language. It appropriately distinguishes industry access from undue influence and existing-law enforcement from passage of AI legislation.

evidence.note: Documents an actual AI voice-cloning attempt to suppress primary voting before publication, supporting the election-interference component.
Documents recurring manipulated-image abuse in 2023, but does not establish widespread deepfake scams as of April 2024.
The advisory board establishes industry participation alongside other interests. Its composition does not establish or disprove undue industry influence over policy.
Supports the limited finding that these protective election bills remained pending. It cannot establish the absence of all qualifying enacted legislation.
Establishes federal protection through application of an existing statute. It qualifies suggestions of total inaction but does not demonstrate passage of protective AI legislation under the contract.

reviews.rationale: Actual AI election interference is supported. The packet does not settle undue industry influence, widespread scam prevalence at publication, or the absence of every qualifying protective federal law. Existing-law enforcement and mixed advisory membership do not decisively contradict the contextual claim. Partial support with unresolved components does not establish the whole observation.
